variations.name: Large light-water reactors (GW-scale new build & restarts)
variations.description: Conventional gigawatt-class pressurized/boiling-water reactors (AP1000, EPR, APR1400, VVER, Hualong One) that split uranium to raise steam at grid scale, plus the new business of restarting recently retired US plants — the workhorse supplying ~9% of world electricity and most of its firm carbon-free power.

companies.name: Westinghouse Electric Company
companies.what: OEM of the AP1000, the only Gen III+ design recently completed in the US (Vogtle 3&4); leading a new US large-reactor build wave.
companies.signal: $80B partnership with US government/Brookfield/Cameco (Oct 2025) targeting 10 new AP1000s under construction by 2030; export pipeline in Poland, Bulgaria, Ukraine.

companies.name: EDF
companies.what: Builds and operates the 1,650 MWe EPR; runs the French fleet and the UK's two flagship new-build projects.
companies.signal: Flamanville-3 EPR reached full power in 2025; Hinkley Point C under construction; Sizewell C (2 EPRs, >$30B) approved with UK government backing in 2025; EPR2 domestic program launched.

companies.name: KHNP (Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power)
companies.what: Exports the APR1400 with a track record of roughly on-time delivery (UAE Barakah 4-unit plant).
companies.signal: Signed ~$18B contract in mid-2025 for two new units at Czech Dukovany, beating EDF and Westinghouse; Korea restarting domestic new build.

companies.name: Rosatom
companies.what: World's largest reactor exporter, building VVER-1200s on a state-financed build-own-operate model.
companies.signal: ~20+ unit export order book including Akkuyu (Turkey, first unit commissioning), El Dabaa (Egypt), India and China — despite sanctions pressure.

companies.name: CNNC / CGN
companies.what: China's state builders of the Hualong One; the fastest and cheapest large-reactor constructors in the world (~6-7 years per unit).
companies.signal: China approving ~10 new reactors per year since 2022 with ~30 units under construction — over half of all global nuclear construction.

companies.name: Holtec International
companies.what: Executing the first-ever restart of a fully retired US nuclear plant — the 800 MW Palisades PWR in Michigan.
companies.signal: $1.52B DOE loan guarantee closed; reactor returned to operating temperature/pressure late 2025 with grid return in early 2026 — first recommissioning in US history.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.what: Largest US nuclear operator; restarting Three Mile Island Unit 1 (renamed Crane Clean Energy Center) on the back of hyperscaler demand.
companies.signal: 20-year Microsoft PPA for the full 835 MW (Sept 2024); $1B federal loan backing (Nov 2025); restart accelerated to 2H 2027.

companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.what: Restarting the ~600 MW Duane Arnold BWR in Iowa — the third US restart project, and the only BWR among them.
companies.signal: Google PPA signed Oct 2025; NRC license-change filings under way since Jan 2025; restart targeted late this decade.

variations.name: Light-water small modular reactors (SMRs)
variations.description: Shrunken, factory-built versions of proven water-cooled reactors (roughly 30-470 MWe) that trade economies of scale for series manufacturing, simpler passive safety, easier siting and smaller per-project capital risk.

companies.name: NuScale Power
companies.what: Holds the only NRC SMR design approvals (50 MWe in 2020, uprated 77 MWe module in May 2025) for its multi-module VOYGR plant.
companies.signal: NYSE: SMR; first project (Utah CFPP) cancelled 2023 on cost escalation — a key cautionary signal; now advancing RoPower (Romania) and a 6 GW ENTRA1/TVA deployment program.

companies.name: GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy
companies.what: BWRX-300 boiling-water SMR — the first SMR under construction in the Western world, at OPG's Darlington site in Ontario.
companies.signal: Canadian construction licence April 2025, first unit in service ~2029-30; follow-on pipeline at TVA Clinch River, Poland (Orlen Synthos) and the UK.

companies.name: Rolls-Royce SMR
companies.what: 470 MWe three-loop PWR derived from UK naval-reactor expertise, designed for factory modules assembled on site.
companies.signal: Selected June 2025 as Great British Energy-Nuclear's preferred bidder for the UK SMR program (initial 3 units); Czech utility CEZ took a ~20% stake.

companies.name: Holtec International
companies.what: SMR-300 pressurized-water SMR, with the first pair sited at its restarted Palisades campus to reuse grid and licensing infrastructure.
companies.signal: Selected for up to $400M of DOE Gen III+ SMR deployment funding (late 2025); targeting ~2030 first units; UK and India partnerships.

companies.name: Westinghouse
companies.what: AP300 — a 330 MWe single-loop derivative of the already-licensed AP1000, betting that licensing reuse beats novel designs.
companies.signal: Design development funded under the Brookfield/Cameco ownership; first deployments targeted early 2030s.

companies.name: CNNC
companies.what: Linglong One (ACP100, 125 MWe) at Changjiang, Hainan — the world's first onshore commercial SMR to finish construction.
companies.signal: Cold functional tests completed Oct 2025; turbine tests passed; commercial operation targeted 2026.

companies.name: Rosatom
companies.what: RITM-200 series PWRs proven on icebreakers and the floating plant Akademik Lomonosov (operating since 2020); now first land-based unit.
companies.signal: RITM-200N SMR under construction in Yakutia targeting 2028; serial reactor production line running.

companies.name: EDF (Nuward)
companies.what: French 2x170 MWe SMR program — rebooted in mid-2024 to a simpler proven-technology design after the original proved too complex.
companies.signal: Design reset of Europe's flagship SMR is direct evidence of LWR-SMR engineering/cost risk; new basic design phase under way.

companies.name: Deep Fission
companies.what: Puts 15 MWe PWR modules at the bottom of 1.6 km boreholes, using rock overburden as the containment to slash plant capex.
companies.signal: Launched ~$150M Nasdaq IPO (ticker FISN) May 2026 at ~$1.66B target valuation; NRC pre-application engagement; data-center LOIs.

variations.name: High-temperature gas-cooled & pebble-bed reactors (HTGR)
variations.description: Helium-cooled reactors fueled with meltdown-tolerant TRISO particle fuel (pebbles or prisms) that run at 565-750°C, opening industrial process-heat and steam markets that water-cooled reactors physically cannot serve.

companies.name: X-energy
companies.what: Xe-100 80 MWe pebble-bed HTGR aimed at industrial steam and data-center power, with vertically integrated TRISO fuel (TRISO-X).
companies.signal: Amazon-backed; $700M Series D (Nov 2025); listed publicly Apr 2026 with shares up 27% on debut; Dow Seadrift 4-unit construction permit application filed with NRC; up to 12 units planned with Energy Northwest.

companies.name: China Huaneng / CNNC / Tsinghua INET
companies.what: Built and operate HTR-PM at Shidao Bay — the world's only operating commercial pebble-bed HTGR (2x250 MWt driving one turbine).
companies.signal: Grid-connected 2021, commercial operation since late 2023; demonstrated inherent-safety shutdown tests; scaled HTR-PM600 planned.

companies.name: Radiant Nuclear
companies.what: 1.2 MWe helium-cooled HTGR microreactor (Kaleidos) — the HTGR concept shrunk to a shipping container (also listed under microreactors).
companies.signal: >$400M raised across Series C ($100M, Jun 2025) and Series D (>$300M); first fueled test at INL's DOME facility in 2026.

companies.name: Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (USNC)
companies.what: Developed the MMR gas-cooled microreactor and proprietary FCM TRISO fuel; was among the best-known Western HTGR ventures.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 in Oct 2024 after capital ran out mid-demonstration; fuel division sold for $28M to Standard Nuclear.

companies.name: U-Battery
companies.what: 4 MWe HTGR micro-reactor consortium incubated by Urenco for off-grid and mining applications.
companies.signal: Wound down March 2023 after Urenco exhausted attempts to find commercial investors; IP transferred to UK National Nuclear Laboratory.

variations.white_space: Only China operates a commercial HTGR, and two Western players (USNC, U-Battery) died in 2023-24 — high-temperature materials and TRISO fuel cost have outrun venture timelines; the opening is decarbonized industrial steam (500-600°C for chemicals/refining) that LWRs can't reach, now de-risked by the rebuilding US TRISO supply chain.

variations.name: Molten salt reactors (incl. thorium fuel cycles)
variations.description: Reactors cooled — or directly fueled — by molten fluoride/chloride salts at near-atmospheric pressure, including thorium breeding cycles, promising walk-away safety, high-temperature output and eventual waste burning, but still proving salt chemistry and fuel qualification at small scale.

companies.name: Kairos Power
companies.what: Fluoride-salt-cooled, TRISO-fueled reactor (FHR); iterating hardware fast with non-nuclear test units before its Hermes demo reactor.
companies.signal: Hermes under construction at Oak Ridge with up to $303M in milestone-based DOE funding; Google master agreement for 500 MW of plants by 2035.

companies.name: Terrestrial Energy
companies.what: Integral Molten Salt Reactor (IMSR) with sealed, swappable 7-year core units producing ~390 MWe per plant.
companies.signal: First publicly traded MSR developer — began trading on Nasdaq (IMSR) Oct 29, 2025 via SPAC with ~$292M gross proceeds; commercial plant sited at Texas A&M-RELLIS.

companies.name: Copenhagen Atomics
companies.what: Mass-manufactured, container-sized thorium molten salt reactors with in-house salt pumps, valves and instrumentation sold as products.
companies.signal: Critical experiment with thorium salt planned at Paul Scherrer Institute ~2026-27 (first in Europe); first chain reaction targeted 2028.

companies.name: Saltfoss Energy (formerly Seaborg Technologies)
companies.what: Compact molten salt reactors for shipyard-built floating power barges (with Samsung Heavy Industries heritage partnership).
companies.signal: Survived a hard restructuring: renamed from Seaborg in Apr 2025 after raising ~DKK 200M; refocused on Denmark/Korea projects.

companies.name: ThorCon
companies.what: 500 MWe shipyard-built molten salt power plant ('thorium converter') towed to shallow-water sites, targeting Indonesia.
companies.signal: Received Indonesia's first-ever nuclear plant licensing approval (BAPETEN site evaluation, Aug 2025); construction possible 2027, full power ~2031.

companies.name: Moltex Energy
companies.what: Stable Salt Reactor-Wasteburner (SSR-W) that runs on transuranics recycled from spent CANDU fuel via its WATSS process.
companies.signal: Demonstrated >95% transuranic extraction from real spent fuel with Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (2025); CNSC pre-licensing; sited at Point Lepreau, New Brunswick.

companies.name: Natura Resources
companies.what: 1 MWt liquid-fueled molten salt research reactor (MSR-1) at Abilene Christian University, with follow-on units aimed at Texas water desalination.
companies.signal: Won the first NRC construction permit ever issued for a liquid-fueled MSR (Sept 2024); Texas legislature funding; DOE enriched-salt allocation secured.

companies.name: SINAP (Shanghai Institute of Applied Physics, CAS)
companies.what: Operates TMSR-LF1, a 2 MWt thorium-bearing molten salt reactor in the Gobi desert — the only operating MSR in the world.
companies.signal: Demonstrated in-core thorium-to-uranium conversion; 10 MWt-class successor and pilot-scale thorium fuel cycle planned.

companies.name: Transatomic Power
companies.what: MIT-spinout MSR startup whose waste-burning claims had to be retracted after neutronics errors.
companies.signal: Shut down in 2018 and open-sourced its IP — the sector's canonical cautionary tale on overstated modeling claims.

companies.name: Flibe Energy
companies.what: Long-running advocate-led venture for the liquid-fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR).
companies.signal: Minimal disclosed funding or hardware progress in 2024-26; commercial viability unclear.

variations.white_space: No Western MSR has yet gone critical — salt corrosion chemistry, liquid-fuel qualification and lack of licensing precedent keep most players pre-criticality, and thorium specifically is led by a Chinese state lab rather than companies; openings exist in salt-side supply chains (pumps, purification, instrumentation) and thorium fuel-cycle IP, where Copenhagen Atomics is nearly alone in the West.

variations.name: Sodium- and lead-cooled fast reactors
variations.description: Liquid-metal-cooled reactors with fast neutron spectra that extract dramatically more energy from uranium and can burn plutonium and nuclear waste; the flagship US advanced build (Natrium) pairs one with molten-salt thermal storage so output can flex around renewables.

companies.name: TerraPower
companies.what: Natrium — 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor with gigawatt-hour molten-salt storage (co-developed with GE Hitachi), under construction at Kemmerer, Wyoming.
companies.signal: Bill Gates-founded; $650M raise in June 2025 incl. NVIDIA's NVentures; NRC construction permit completed Dec 2025-early 2026 (first for a US commercial advanced reactor); operation ~2030.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.what: Aurora — liquid-metal-cooled fast microreactor running on HALEU (and eventually recycled fuel), sold as power-as-a-service.
companies.signal: NYSE: OKLO (Sam Altman-backed, stock ~$70-80 in Apr 2026); first Aurora under construction at INL targeting first operations by end-2027; NRC approved its principal design criteria; multi-GW data-center and USAF pipeline.

companies.name: newcleo
companies.what: Lead-cooled fast reactors (LFR-AS-200) designed to run on MOX fuel made from reprocessed nuclear waste, closing the fuel cycle in Europe.
companies.signal: Europe's best-funded nuclear startup (>€500M raised since 2021); France/Italy/UK footprint; materials R&D partnership with Blykalla (2025).

companies.name: ARC Clean Technology
companies.what: ARC-100 sodium-cooled fast reactor based directly on the 30-year EBR-II operating record, sited at Point Lepreau, New Brunswick.
companies.signal: New capital raised in 2025; collaboration with KHNP; CNSC vendor design review progressing.

companies.name: Blykalla
companies.what: Swedish KTH spinout building SEALER, a small lead-cooled reactor using proprietary corrosion-resistant steels.
companies.signal: Raised $50M in Dec 2025 to accelerate its SMR for data centers; electric (non-nuclear) prototype testing under way.

companies.name: Hexana
companies.what: French startup (ASTRID program heritage) pairing twin 400 MWt sodium fast reactors with high-temperature heat storage for industrial sites.
companies.signal: €25M raised Jan 2025 (equity + France 2030 grant); entered preparatory regulatory review with French regulator ASNR; Tractebel partnership.

companies.name: Rosatom
companies.what: Only operator of commercial fast reactors — BN-600 and BN-800 sodium units at Beloyarsk — and building the BREST-OD-300 lead-cooled demo with on-site fuel recycling at Seversk.
companies.signal: Decades of sodium fast-reactor operating hours; BN-800 running on full MOX core; BREST targeted for late-2020s startup.

companies.name: CNNC
companies.what: CFR-600 sodium-cooled fast reactor at Xiapu (grid-connected demonstration) as a step to a CFR-1000 commercial breeder fleet.
companies.signal: CFR-600 operating/commissioning since 2023-24; second unit under construction; closed-fuel-cycle national strategy.

variations.white_space: Operating experience is concentrated in Russia and China — the West dismantled its fast-reactor base after the 1994 IFR cancellation — and every Western startup is gated by HALEU/plutonium fuel availability; the opening is waste-burning economics (paid twice: for disposal relief and power) and supplying the sodium/lead component chain Natrium is now creating.

variations.name: Microreactors (heat-pipe, transportable)
variations.description: Container-sized reactors from ~100 kW to ~20 MW, built whole in factories and trucked (or flown) to site to replace diesel generators at remote communities, mines, military bases and data centers; first fueled demonstrations begin in 2026 at INL's DOME test bed.

companies.name: Radiant Nuclear
companies.what: Kaleidos — 1.2 MWe helium-cooled microreactor in a shipping container, mass-production-first business model (50 units/yr factory goal).
companies.signal: $100M Series C (Jun 2025) then >$300M Series D within ~6 months; first fueled microreactor test at INL DOME in 2026; USAF deal to deploy at Eielson AFB.

companies.name: Westinghouse (eVinci)
companies.what: 5 MWe heat-pipe microreactor with no pumps or water — sodium heat pipes passively move heat from a TRISO core for 8+ years per fueling.
companies.signal: Selected alongside Radiant as the first two DOME test campaigns starting spring 2026; agreements in Saskatchewan and at Penn State.

companies.name: BWXT
companies.what: Project Pele — the US DoD's transportable TRISO-fueled microreactor prototype, plus the commercial BANR variant.
companies.signal: ~$300M DoD contract; full TRISO core fuel delivered to INL Dec 2025 with assembly and testing in 2026 — likely the first new-design US microreactor to operate.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.what: Aurora 15-75 MWe fast microreactor 'powerhouse' sold on a build-own-operate power-as-a-service model (also listed under fast reactors).
companies.signal: First commercial unit under construction at INL targeting power by end-2027; NYSE: OKLO with multi-billion market cap.

companies.name: Aalo Atomics
companies.what: Aalo-1 10 MWe sodium-cooled microreactor (DOE MARVEL lineage) clustered into 'Aalo Pods' — power plants co-built with the data center they feed.
companies.signal: $100M Series B (Aug 2025, Valor Equity/NRG); broke ground on Aalo-X experimental reactor at INL with criticality targeted 2026; first US advanced-fuel purchase deal.

companies.name: Last Energy
companies.what: Steel-encased 5-20 MWe micro-PWRs (PWR-5/PWR-20) using only proven LWR technology, sold as modular factory products for industrial parks.
companies.signal: $100M Series C (Dec 2025, Astera Institute); PWR-5 pilot at Texas A&M-RELLIS targeting criticality mid-2026; dozens of European/UK MOUs and a 30-plant Texas plan.

companies.name: Antares
companies.what: R1 — 100 kWe-1 MWe rapidly deployable microreactor aimed at defense, remote and space applications.
companies.signal: $30M Series A (Oct 2024) + $96M Series B (Dec 2025, Shine Capital); NRC pre-application engagement.

companies.name: NANO Nuclear Energy
companies.what: Publicly listed microreactor developer (KRONOS MMR at University of Illinois; ZEUS portable concept) plus HALEU logistics ambitions.
companies.signal: NASDAQ: NNE with ~$569M liquidity (Mar 2026) after a $400M placement; KRONOS construction permit application submitted to NRC, construction from ~2027.

companies.name: Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (USNC)
companies.what: Was a leading microreactor developer (MMR projects in Canada and Illinois) before its 2024 collapse.
companies.signal: Chapter 11 in Oct 2024 — evidence that microreactor capital intensity can outrun milestone revenue; assets dispersed at auction.

variations.name: Fuel cycle & enrichment (HALEU, TRISO, fabrication)
variations.description: The mining-to-fabrication supply chain — especially uranium enrichment and the HALEU (10-20% enriched) and TRISO particle fuels that advanced reactors require — being urgently rebuilt in the West after the 2024 US ban on Russian uranium imports.

companies.name: Centrus Energy
companies.what: Operates America's only licensed HALEU production line (Piketon, Ohio) with US-origin centrifuge technology.
companies.signal: Delivered 900 kg HALEU to DOE by mid-2025; won a $900M DOE task order plus announced multi-billion-dollar Piketon expansion; NYSE: LEU.

companies.name: Urenco
companies.what: One of the world's largest enrichers; expanding its Eunice, New Mexico plant and adding HALEU capability in the US and UK.
companies.signal: First new cascade of a 15% capacity expansion online May 2025 (complete 2027); selected under DOE's $2.7B LEU+HALEU program.

companies.name: Orano
companies.what: French fuel-cycle major (Georges Besse II enrichment, conversion, La Hague recycling) now siting a new US centrifuge plant.
companies.signal: $900M DOE enrichment task order to Orano Federal Services (Jan 2026); Oak Ridge, TN selected for US expansion.

companies.name: General Matter
companies.what: SpaceX-alumni-founded startup building dedicated HALEU enrichment capacity on the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant site.
companies.signal: Emerged from stealth Apr 2025; DOE site lease Aug 2025; $900M DOE production award Jan 2026 — fastest-rising new entrant in enrichment.

companies.name: Global Laser Enrichment (Silex/Cameco JV)
companies.what: Commercializing SILEX laser enrichment — a third-generation technology that can also re-enrich DOE's depleted uranium tails at Paducah.
companies.signal: Technology demo milestones passed; received a $28.5M DOE award (sought $900M) and is advancing the Paducah Laser Enrichment Facility.

companies.name: X-energy (TRISO-X)
companies.what: Building TF3 in Oak Ridge — the first commercial-scale TRISO fuel fabrication facility in North America.
companies.signal: Vertically integrates fuel for its Xe-100 fleet and third parties; backed by X-energy's $700M Series D and 2026 public listing.

companies.name: Standard Nuclear
companies.what: Bought bankrupt USNC's TRISO fuel assets for $28M and restarted production (~500 kg/yr) in Oak Ridge as an independent merchant fuel supplier.
companies.signal: $140M Series A (Jan 2026); joined DOE's advanced fuel pilot program; >$100M in projected 2027 fuel sales.

companies.name: BWXT
companies.what: Sole maker of US naval reactor fuel; restarted the first US TRISO production line and supplies defense and microreactor fuel.
companies.signal: Delivered the complete TRISO core for Project Pele (Dec 2025); NNSA defense fuels contracts; expanding Lynchburg capacity.

companies.name: Lightbridge
companies.what: Developing metallic HALEU fuel rods that boost power and safety margins in existing LWRs and SMRs.
companies.signal: NASDAQ: LTBR; fabrication and irradiation work with DOE/INL progressing; long pre-revenue.

companies.name: Cameco
companies.what: One of the world's largest uranium miners and fuel-services providers; 49% owner of Westinghouse and GLE stakeholder, spanning the whole front end.
companies.signal: Ramping McArthur River/Cigar Lake output into a post-Russian-ban uranium bull market; party to the $80B US AP1000 partnership.

variations.white_space: Post-2024 enrichment is suddenly crowded with DOE money, but uranium conversion/deconversion remains effectively single-source in the US (Honeywell's Metropolis plant) and TRISO kernel feedstock is a chokepoint — unglamorous mid-chain steps are the clearest opening for new entrants.

variations.name: Waste disposal & recycling
variations.description: Engineered disposal of spent fuel (deep geological repositories, deep boreholes, dry-cask interim storage) and chemical recycling that recovers the ~95% of energy still in used fuel — the unsolved back end that gates public acceptance and now doubles as a domestic HALEU feedstock source.

companies.name: Posiva
companies.what: Operating Onkalo in Finland — the world's first deep geological repository for spent fuel, using the KBS-3 copper-canister method.
companies.signal: Final disposal trial runs completed 2024-25; routine operations expected mid-decade — the global proof point that permanent disposal is doable.

companies.name: SKB
companies.what: Swedish counterpart building the Forsmark spent-fuel repository and Oskarshamn encapsulation plant on the same KBS-3 method.
companies.signal: Repository construction began 2025 after final court clearances; ~70-year operating program.

companies.name: Orano
companies.what: Runs La Hague, the West's only commercial-scale reprocessing complex (~1,100 tHM/yr), plus MOX fabrication and US dry storage (NUHOMS).
companies.signal: Partnering with SHINE on US recycling pilots; La Hague life-extension investment under way.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.what: Building the first phase of a commercial US fuel recycling campus (electrorefining/pyroprocessing) to turn spent LWR fuel into fast-reactor fuel.
companies.signal: Announced up to $1.68B advanced fuel center in Oak Ridge, TN (2025); among five firms negotiating DOE surplus-plutonium allocations.

companies.name: Curio
companies.what: NuCycle chemical recycling process designed to cut high-level waste volume to ~4% while recovering reactor fuel and valuable isotopes.
companies.signal: Lab-scale demonstrations with DOE national labs; selected for DOE recycling/plutonium negotiations; gained White House attention in late 2025.

companies.name: SHINE Technologies
companies.what: Fusion-neutron isotope producer using its irradiation/chemistry base as a stepping stone to a commercial spent-fuel recycling pilot (~2030 target).
companies.signal: Recycling pilot agreement with Orano; DOE grant for recycling process design incorporating transport/storage/disposal.

companies.name: Deep Isolation
companies.what: Disposes of spent fuel and HLW in deep horizontal boreholes drilled with oil-and-gas directional techniques — repository safety without a mined repository.
companies.signal: DOE-funded canister and demonstration work; international pilots (incl. Estonia) and IAEA engagement.

companies.name: Moltex Energy
companies.what: WATSS process recycles spent CANDU fuel into fast-reactor fuel, paired with its waste-burning SSR-W reactor (also listed under MSRs).
companies.signal: >95% transuranic recovery shown on real used fuel with CNL (2025); CNSC pre-licensing consultation under way.

companies.name: Holtec International
companies.what: Dominant supplier of spent-fuel dry-cask storage worldwide and holder of an NRC license for a consolidated interim storage facility in New Mexico.
companies.signal: Thousands of casks deployed; CISF licensed but politically stalled — a live marker of US back-end gridlock.

companies.name: EnergySolutions
companies.what: Operates major US low-level waste disposal (Clive, Utah) and a large reactor decommissioning business.
companies.signal: Steady disposal/decommissioning revenue; positioned for the restart-era waste logistics market.

variations.white_space: Disposal is a government-monopoly market where the US has had no repository path since Yucca Mountain stalled, and recycling has historically lost to cheap fresh uranium plus proliferation concerns; the opening is recycling reframed as HALEU feedstock and waste-liability relief (Oklo/Curio model), plus borehole disposal for countries too small to afford a mined repository.
